I fixed the error by allowing cleartext HTTP to `10.0.2.2` in debug builds only. I could not build or run the app here, so this is verified by reading the files, not by a test run.

**Cause:** The debug build sets `API_BASE_URL` to `http://10.0.2.2:8080/` (`app/build.gradle.kts:19`). Since Android 9 (API 28), apps block cleartext HTTP unless a network security config allows it. The manifest had none, so OkHttp's connection was refused.

**Changes:**
- **`app/src/debug/res/xml/network_security_config.xml`** (new): a config with a `domain-config` that sets `cleartextTrafficPermitted="true"` for the domain `10.0.2.2` only.
- **`app/src/debug/AndroidManifest.xml`** (new): a debug manifest overlay that sets `android:networkSecurityConfig="@xml/network_security_config"` on `<application>`. Gradle merges it into the debug variant only.

I put these in the `debug` source set rather than `main`, so release builds (which use `https://api.shelftap.example/`) keep the default HTTPS-only policy.

Rebuild and run the debug variant to confirm the `catalog failed` error is gone. The backend at `10.0.2.2:8080` also needs to be running on the host.
